newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Branson balloon readied for around world flight. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Branson balloon readied for around world flight. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]

text.p: Technicians were inflating the balloon in which British tycoon Richard Branson planned on Tuesday to launch his bid to become the first balloonist to make a round-the-world trip.
The launch was now expected to take place between 0700 and 0900 GMT on Tuesday instead of between 0630 and 0730 GMT as originally thought, Branson said.
The huge balloon, called Virgin Global Challenger, was hauled from a warehouse in a military airbase in Marrakesh for a 12-hour countdown to take-off.

"We got the green light for an early departure...We have the best chance in the last five years for good weather conditions. We expect to take off around 0700 and 0900 GMT on Tuesday," Branson told reporters in a night briefing.
"It is a complicated operation to assemble the huge balloon...In fact, it takes more time," he said.
The flight is estimated to take between 14 and 21 days, with a "realistic" expected time of about 18 days.
More than 300 Moroccan soldiers were mobilised to help the 40 British technicians assemble the balloon, officials said.

The balloon, which will be filled by 1.1 million cubic feet (30,000 cubic metres) of combined helium and hot air, will climb to 30,000 feet (10,000 metres) over the snow-capped Atlas mountains, Branson said.

The 194.8-foot (59.38-metre) balloon was constructed of fabric specifically designed for the project. The laminated envelope is made from a high-tenacity polyamide fabric coated with a polyurethane compound.
"It is specifically laminated to produce maximum ultra-violet protection while reducing gas losses through porosity by a factor of 10," a British technician said.
Branson, the flamboyant 46-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies, is accompanied by his two co-pilots Per Lindstrand and Rory Mc Carthy.
He said earlier he was "confident that the trip will take place tomorrow...But cannot forecast the weather conditions more six days ahead".
Virgin Global Challenger is the second balloon to be prepared for Branson's attempt. Bad weather last year forced the tycoon to put off a planned flight in another craft.
The red-walled tourist city of Marrakesh has been chosen as the ideal launch pad as it is on the faster, southerly sub-tropical jet stream rather than the northern polar stream.
Speed is essential as Branson is racing against American balloonist Steve Fosset and a two-man team planning a launch from St. Louis, Missouri in the United States.
(Corrects Fosset's launch location from Switzerland).
"I am aware of the competition but I can assure you that we will be one or two days ahead of Steve Fosset," Branson said.
The three-man crew spent three days training in the new balloon in December and have been waiting since for ideal weather.

The balloon flight is the latest in a series of record breaking attempts that have indulged Branson's taste for adventure while earning publicity for his businesses ranging from Virgin Atlantic Airways to contraceptives.
Branson's two children, Sam and Sally, aged 11 and 15, followed the final preparations with great interest.
"They came here to Marrakesh to attend the final launch of Virgin Global Challenger because it is a great adventure for them as well," Branson added.
